assumptions.text: Delivery is incremental: text chunks and tool status updates are emitted as events and followed by one terminal completion, so no caller waits for the full answer.
assumptions.source: streams its answer back word by word in real time

assumptions.text: The directed capability is a single conversational agent with a bounded tool loop, not a multi-agent topology, so no delegation edge exists.
assumptions.source: the agent thinks through the request, calls backend tools when it needs real data or actions

assumptions.text: No backend tool is declared as high-impact or irreversible and no approval resume surface exists, so no approval gate is planned.
Conversation memory is kept per session as the last 12 messages verbatim plus a rolling summary persisted in the store, within the 16,000-token limit.

capabilities.requirement: The answer reaches the caller as incremental text chunk and tool status events followed by a terminal completion event.

measurement.assertion: A stub emitting N chunks yields N chunk events then exactly one terminal completion event, observed without waiting for full completion first.

capabilities.requirement: Every tool the model requests passes the same session ownership admission as the human path, only enumerated tools are callable, and a turn makes at most 5 tool calls.

measurement.assertion: A stub requesting a non-enumerated tool or a sixth call yields zero extra tool invocations and a clean stop notice.

capabilities.requirement: A model failure or the 30-second turn timeout degrades to an honest refusal notice in the stream instead of an unhandled error.

measurement.assertion: A failing stub yields one refusal notice event, one terminal completion and no further model calls.

capabilities.requirement: The generation prompt is a versioned source type whose members are version, role identity, input placeholders, output-schema reference and refusal text.

measurement.assertion: The prompt source type exposes all five members non-empty and the rendered prompt contains every declared placeholder.

capabilities.requirement: A tool-call request emitted by the model is schema-validated before execution and a violation is refused, never coerced.

measurement.assertion: A stub returning a malformed tool request executes zero tools and yields a refusal outcome.

capabilities.requirement: Every context assembly keeps the last 12 messages verbatim and older content only as the rolling summary within the 16,000-token limit.

measurement.assertion: An assembled window over more than 12 messages holds exactly 12 verbatim messages and a token count at or below the configured limit.

capabilities.requirement: Memory is durable per session, bounded by a rolling summary updated idempotently by session id and turn id, and never shared across sessions.

measurement.assertion: Replaying the same turn completion twice calls the summarizer stub once and leaves one summary row for the session.

capabilities.requirement: A turn has a token budget per call taken from configuration with a named over-budget behavior of stopping cleanly and informing the user.

measurement.assertion: The budget is read from a named configuration key and a stub exceeding it ends the turn with the stop notice.

capabilities.requirement: Conversational behavior is pinned by a versioned golden example set of input and expected property run offline against the stub port.

measurement.assertion: Every golden example runs against the stub and satisfies its expected property such as chunk count, tool-call count or refusal.

invariants.rule: Every model access is a port with an offline stand-in that takes precedence over the production adapter, and no unit test, slice or boot reaches a live endpoint.
The think-and-call-tool cycle of a turn is capped at 5 tool calls and 30 seconds and ends with the named cycle-break outcome of a clean stop notice to the user.

duties.obligation: Deliver the AR-01 answer as chunk and status events then one terminal completion over a non-blocking channel.
Admit each AR-01 tool request only for enumerated tools after the same ownership check as the human path.
Route an AR-01 failure or timeout to an honest refusal notice with a declared trigger.
Hold the versioned prompt as a source type with version, role identity, input placeholders, output-schema reference and refusal text members.
Validate each AR-01 tool request against its schema before execution and refuse violations.
Assemble the context window with the 12-message and 16,000-token bounds read from configuration.
Persist the rolling summary per session with idempotent update, using AR-02 to condense older turns for AR-01.
Enforce the configured per-turn token budget with the stop-and-inform behavior when exceeded.
Provide an offline harness that runs the versioned golden set against the stub port.
Provide offline stand-ins for the AR-01 and AR-02 ports that win precedence in every test context, proved by the context resolving the port to the stand-in.
Bound the AR-01 tool cycle by a max-turns count and a clean-stop outcome proved by stub call count.

risks.risk: A live model call from a test or boot would bill real tokens and make results non-deterministic.
A tool-calling cycle could spin without end while each call stays small and valid.
A time-to-first-token stall would make the interface feel slow.
Tool calls with side effects are not undone when a turn is cut at a limit.
risks.mitigation: accepted: the turn stops cleanly and informs the user
risks.residual: Side effects of tools already executed before the cut remain.

risks.risk: Message size, summary length and retention are unbounded by the inputs.
